docs.title: Gothic 2 Online – CEF Module
docs.text: This module integrates the Chromium Embedded Framework (CEF) into Gothic 2 Online, enabling in-game browsers and frontend UI using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Embed Chromium-based browsers into the game.
  • Control browser properties and behavior via Squirrel scripts.
  • Call JavaScript functions from Squirrel and vice versa.
  • Support for custom protocols.
  • Audio support with volume and mute control.

docs.title: class Browser (client-side)
docs.text:
Available since version: 1.0.0

This class represents CEF browser on the screen.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
Browser(int x, int y, int width, int height, string url, bool useAcceleratedMode = true)

Parameters:

  • int x: the x position in virtuals.
  • int y: the y position in virtuals.
  • int width: the width size in virtuals.
  • int height: the height size in virtuals.
  • string url: the url to be navigated to.
  • bool useAcceleratedMode: Enables hardware-accelerated rendering. When enabled, browser frames are transferred using shared GPU textures, providing better performance than CPU-based rendering. Requires DirectX 11 and is automatically disabled on Wine or unsupported systems.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: If for some reason typed characters are being improperly displayed for you, please make sure that your Active Code Page is properly set in windows registry.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Create a file called acp.reg on your desktop
  • Open up with notepad or any other text editor
  • Paste the below code into this value, also, make sure to set the ACP value to proper one based on the example table below
Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Nls\CodePage]
"ACP"="1250"
Code Page Region / Script Supported Languages 1250 Central & Eastern Europe Czech, Polish, Slovak, Hungarian, Slovene, Serbo-Croatian (Latin), Romanian (pre-1993), Albanian, German, English 1251 Cyrillic Russian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian, Serbian (Cyrillic), Macedonian 1252 Western Europe English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Scandinavian languages 1253 Greek Greek 1254 Turkish Turkish 1255 Hebrew Hebrew 1256 Arabic Arabic 1257 Baltic Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian 1258 Vietnamese Vietnamese

docs.title: Alternative solution (Windows system locale)
docs.text: If changing the Active Code Page (ACP) does not resolve the issue, the problem may be related to how Windows handles non-Unicode programs.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Open Control Panel
  • Go to: Region → Administrative
  • Click: Change system locale...

  • Set: Current system locale: Polish (Poland) (or another locale matching your language)

  • (Optional but recommended) Disable: Beta: Use Unicode UTF-8 for worldwide language support This option may cause incorrect character rendering in older applications.

  • Click OK

  • Restart your computer

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
If you get errors like this one: 

[34324:27692:0924/212531.059:ERROR:validation_errors.cc(117)] Invalid message: VALIDATION_ERROR_DESERIALIZATION_FAILED
[34324:27692:0924/212531.059:ERROR:render_process_host_impl.cc(5509)] Terminating render process for bad Mojo message: Received bad user message: Validation failed for content.mojom.FrameHost.6  [VALIDATION_ERROR_DESERIALIZATION_FAILED]
[34324:27692:0924/212531.059:ERROR:bad_message.cc(29)] Terminating renderer for bad IPC message, reason 123
[34324:27692:0924/212531.060:ERROR:interface_endpoint_client.cc(725)] Message 1805668172 rejected by interface content.mojom.FrameHost

Then most likely you're using incompatible cef-launcher.exe with CEF.dll.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text: Reinstall CEF by reinstalling the Gothic 2 Online Mod.

docs.title: 🌐 Supported protocols
docs.text: The CEF Module supports the following protocols:

docs.title: file
docs.text: The file:// protocol is only supported for the server that is using <debug>true</debug>. It can be used to quickly test the changes in your local .html, .js, .css files.

docs.title: cef
docs.text:
The cef:// protocol works similar to the file://, however instead of reading files from physical file path, we are reading them by using Gothic Virtual File System.

In order to make your website available through this protocol you need to put it into this directory: - _WORK/DATA/WEB/.

You can also create subdirectories in this directory, keep in mind that only .zip archive supports nested structure, using .vdf to pack resources is heavilly discouraged due to float format structure (only one file with given name can be resolved)

docs.title: vdfs
docs.text: The vdfs:// protocol is mostly the same as cef:// with one important difference, it uses absolute game path as base directory, meaning that you can load the gothic assets via CEF like this: vdfs://_work/data/meshes/_compiled/skull.mrm.

docs.title: Example directories
docs.text:
• cef://index.html (located in _WORK/DATA/WEB/INDEX.HTML)
  • cef://site/index.html (located in _WORK/DATA/WEB/SITE/INDEX.HTML)

docs.title: http & https
docs.text: The http:// and https:// protocol is supported, however only certain websites are white listed. This is because public access to any type of public website might be used to scam other ppl or hijack their login & password by making official websites clones.

docs.title: We currently allow connecting to these websites:
docs.text:
• 127.0.0.*
  • localhost
  • youtube.com
  • *.youtube.com
  • youtube-nocookie.com
  • google.com
  • *.google.com
  • imgur.com
  • *.imgur.com

docs.title: 🟨 JavaScript -> Squirrel communication 🐿️
docs.text:
The squirrel namespace is a bridge from the JavaScript side of the engine into Squirrel scripting. It allows you to:

  • Call Squirrel functions from JavaScript
  • Pass arguments between frontend and backend logic
  • Receive return values from game logic, player state, etc.

docs.title: Declaration:
docs.text: squirrel.call(functionName: string, args?: any): Promise<any>

docs.title: Arguments:
docs.text:
• functionName: name of the function defined in Squirrel
  • args: optional payload (object, string, number, etc.)
  • Returns a Promise resolving with the function’s return value

docs.title: 📝 Practical Examples Using squirrel.call(...)
docs.text: This guide walks through common patterns of using squirrel.call(...) in JavaScript to interact with server logic written in Squirrel.

docs.title: ⚔️ Example 1: Fetch Player Stats
docs.text:
JavaScript requests player stats from Squirrel and shows the result in the DOM elements. Useful for profile views or status HUDs.

HTML: 

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8">
        <script src="script.js" defer></script>
    </head>
    <body>
        <h2>⚔️ Fetch Player Stats</h2>
        <button onclick="fetchStats()">Get Player Stats</button>

        <div id="stats-container">
        <p>Name: <span id="stat-name">—</span></p>
        <p>Level: <span id="stat-level">—</span></p>
        <p>HP: <span id="stat-hp">—</span></p>
        </div>
    </body>
</html>

JS: 

async function fetchStats()
{
    const stats = await squirrel.call("getPlayerStats");
    document.getElementById("stat-name").textContent  = stats.get("name");
    document.getElementById("stat-level").textContent = stats.get("level");
    document.getElementById("stat-hp").textContent    = stats.get("hp");
}

Squirrel: 

function getPlayerStats()
{
    return {
        name = "Diego",
        level = 12,
        hp = 80
    }
}

docs.title: 🔐 Example 2: Login System
docs.text:
Validate credentials and show success or error in separate elements.

HTML: 

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8">
        <script src="script.js" defer></script>
    </head>
    <body>
        <h2>🔐 Login Panel</h2>
        <div id="login-form">
            <label>
                Username:
                <input type="text" id="username" placeholder="Username">
            </label><br>
            <label>
                Password:
                <input type="password" id="password" placeholder="Password">
            </label><br>
            <button onclick="loginUser()">Log In</button>
        </div>

        <div id="login-response">
            <p>Status: <span id="login-status">—</span></p>
            <p>Message: <span id="login-message">—</span></p>
        </div>
    </body>
</html>

JS: 

async function loginUser()
{
    const username = document.getElementById("username").value;
    const password = document.getElementById("password").value;

    const result = await squirrel.call("validateLogin", username, password);

    if (result.get("success"))
    {
        document.getElementById("login-status").textContent  = "Success";
        document.getElementById("login-message").textContent = `Welcome, ${username}!`;
    }
    else
    {
        document.getElementById("login-status").textContent  = "Failure";
        document.getElementById("login-message").textContent = result.get("message");
    }
}

Squirrel: 

function validateLogin(username, password)
{
    if (username == "user" && password == "123")
        return { success = true }
    else
        return { success = false, message = "Invalid credentials." }
}

docs.title: 📝 Practical Examples Using browser::call(...)
docs.text: This guide demonstrates how to invoke frontend JavaScript directly from Squirrel scripts using browser.call(funcName, ...args).

docs.title: 💬 Example 1: Appending Chat Lines
docs.text:
Squirrel emits chat messages that are send to frontend and rendered into a chat container.

Squirrel: 

local browser = Browser(0, 0, 8192, 8192, "cef://site/index.html")

addEventHandler("onPlayerMessage", function(pid, r, g, b, message)
{
    local name = getPlayerName(pid)
    local color = getPlayerColor(pid)

    browser.call("appendChatLine", name, color, msg)
})

HTML: 

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8">
        <script src="script.js" defer></script>
        <style>
            #chat-container
            {
                border:1px solid #ccc;
                padding:10px;
                height:150px;
                overflow-y:auto;
            }
        </style>
    </head>
    <body>
        <h2>Chat Window</h2>
        <div id="chat-container">
            <!-- Chat lines will appear here -->
        </div>
    </body>
</html>

JS: 

function appendChatLine(name, color, message)
{
    const container = document.getElementById("chat-container");
    const line = document.createElement("p");

    // Create name span
    const nameSpan = document.createElement("span");
    nameSpan.textContent = name;
    nameSpan.style.color = `rgb(${color.get("r")}, ${color.get("g")}, ${color.get("b")})`;

    // Create text node for message
    const messageNode = document.createTextNode(": " + message);

    // Build the chat line
    line.appendChild(nameSpan);
    line.appendChild(messageNode);

    // Add line to chat
    container.appendChild(line);
    container.scrollTop = container.scrollHeight;
};

docs.title: ❤️ Example 2: Updating Health Bar from Squirrel
docs.text:
Squirrel reacts to engine-side events (like damage or healing) and pushes updates to the frontend UI using browser.call(...).

Squirrel: 

local browser = Browser(0, 0, 8192, 8192, "cef://site/index.html")

addEventHandler("onPlayerChangeHealth", function(playerId, oldHP, newHP)
{
    if (playerId != heroId)
        return

    local maxHP = getPlayerMaxHealth(playerId)

    browser.call("updateHealthBar", newHP, maxHP)
})

HTML: 

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <script src="script.js" defer></script>
    <style>
        #health-bar-container
        {
            width: 200px;
            height: 20px;
            border: 2px solid #e0e0e0;
            background-color: #717171;
            border-radius: 6px;
            overflow: hidden;
        }

        #health-bar
        {
            width: 100%;
            height: 100%;
            background-color: red;
            transition: width 0.3s ease;
        }
    </style>
</head>

<body>
    <h2>❤️ Player Health</h2>
    <div id="health-bar-container">
        <div id="health-bar"></div>
    </div>
</body>
</html>

JS: 

function updateHealthBar(health, maxHealth)
{
    health = Math.max(0, Math.min(health, maxHealth));
    const percentage = (health / maxHealth) * 100;

    const bar = document.getElementById("health-bar");
    bar.style.width = percentage + "%";
}

docs.title: 🟦 Squirrel -> JavaScript async bridge 🔁
docs.text:
The JSPromise class allows Squirrel code to return a deferred result to JavaScript via a Promise. This is especially useful when your Squirrel logic involves timers, async I/O, or multi-step operations that don’t complete immediately.

It works by creating a native JS Promise object on the frontend, and exposing a handle in Squirrel that can later resolve or reject it.

docs.title: Declaration:
docs.text: local promise = JSPromise()

docs.title: Properties:
docs.text: • valid: true if the promise is still linked to a JS object, otherwise false

docs.title: Methods:
docs.text:
• resolve(result: any): resolves the JS promise with a value
  • reject(error: string): rejects the JS promise with an error message

docs.title: 🕓 Example: Delayed resolution via timer
docs.text:
Squirrel: 

function delayedHello()
{
  local promise = JSPromise()

  setTimer(function() {
    promise.resolve("Hello from Squirrel!")
  }, 1000, 1)

  return promise
}
JavaScript: 
squirrel.call("delayedHello").then(msg => {
  console.log(msg) // "Hello from Squirrel!" (after 1 second)
})

docs.title: 🧠 Why use JSPromise?
docs.text:
• ✅ Enables async workflows in Squirrel that JS can await
  • ✅ Clean separation between logic and timing
  • ✅ Works seamlessly with squirrel.call(...)x Promise interface

docs.title: ⚠️ Notes
docs.text:
• You must call resolve() or reject() manually — otherwise the JS promise will remain pending forever.
  • Once resolved or rejected, the valid property becomes false.

docs.title: 📡 Remote debugger
docs.text: You can remotely debug your ingame website by connecting to it. NOTE! This option is only available if your server has <debug>true</debug> enabled.

docs.title: To do that you need to:
docs.text:
• Open up the chromium based browser
  • Open this url: chrome://inspect#devices
  • Check Discover network targets
  • (optional) Make sure that in Configure.. popup list you have this entry localhost:9222

Once you do that, you just need to click inspect on your website file in Remote Target section.
